facts.statement: Fossils of Bagaceratops have been found in the Barun Goyot and Bayan Mandahu Formations.
facts.quote: Bagaceratops remains have been reported from the Barun Goyot Formation and Bayan Mandahu Formation.

facts.statement: One specimen suggests that Bagaceratops may also have lived in the Djadochta Formation.
facts.quote: One specimen may argue the possible presence of Bagaceratops in the Djadochta Formation.

facts.statement: Bagaceratops lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 72 to 71 million years ago.
facts.quote: Bagaceratops (meaning "small-horned face") is a genus of small protoceratopsid dinosaurs that lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous, around 72 to 71 million years ago.

facts.statement: Bagaceratops was one of the smallest ceratopsians, reaching lengths of 1 to 1.5 meters and weighing between 22.7 and 45 kilograms.
facts.quote: Bagaceratops was among the smallest ceratopsians, growing up to 1 - 1.5 m in length, with a weight about 22.7 - 45 kg.

facts.statement: Unlike its relative Protoceratops, Bagaceratops lacked premaxillary teeth.
facts.quote: Unlike its close relative, Protoceratops, Bagaceratops lacked premaxillary teeth (cylindrical, blunt teeth near the tip of the upper jaw).

facts.statement: The genus Bagaceratops was named in 1975 by Polish paleontologists Teresa Maryańska and Halszka Osmólska.
facts.quote: In 1975, two of the expedition's leading scientists, namely Polish paleontologists Teresa Maryańska and Halszka Osmólska, published a large monograph dedicated to describe this material where they named the new genus and type species of protoceratopsid Bagaceratops rozhdestvenskyi.

facts.statement: The name Bagaceratops means "small-horned face", derived from Mongolian and Greek words.
facts.quote: The generic name, Bagaceratops, means "small-horned face" and is derived from the Mongolian baga = meaning small; and Greek ceratops = meaning horn face.

facts.statement: An articulated and nearly complete Bagaceratops skeleton was collected in 1993 from the Barun Goyot Formation.
facts.quote: In 1993, the Japan-Mongolia Joint Paleontological Expedition collected an articulated and nearly complete Bagaceratops skeleton (MPC-D 100/535) from the Barun Goyot Formation at the Hermiin Tsav locality.

facts.statement: Evidence of invertebrate scavengers on the joints of a Bagaceratops skeleton was analyzed in 2010 and 2011.
facts.quote: In 2010 and 2011 this specimen was examined to analyze several borings (tunnel-like holes) left by invertebrate scavengers on joint areas.

facts.statement: Adult Bagaceratops reached lengths of about 1 to 1.5 meters and weighed between 22.7 and 45 kilograms.
facts.quote: Bagaceratops was a small-sized protoceratopsid, reaching adult dimensions of about 1 - 1.5 m in length and 22.7 - 45 kg in body mass based on Maginostris.

facts.statement: Bagaceratops possessed fused nasal bones and an accessory antorbital fenestra in the maxilla.
facts.quote: Bagaceratops lacked primitive premaxillary teeth, had paired (fused) nasal bones, and an oval-shaped fenestra (hole) was developed in the maxilla—otherwise known as accessory antorbital fenestra.

facts.statement: Bagaceratops belonged to the group Ceratopsia, which included herbivorous dinosaurs with parrot-like beaks.
facts.quote: Bagaceratops belonged to Ceratopsia, a group of herbivorous dinosaurs with parrot-like beaks which thrived in North America and Asia during the Cretaceous Period, which ended roughly 66 million years ago.

facts.statement: Some researchers consider Breviceratops a distinct genus separate from Bagaceratops and Protoceratops due to its mix of primitive and advanced traits.
facts.quote: He also considered Breviceratops to be a distinct and separate genus of protoceratopsid, from both Bagaceratops and Protoceratops, as it features a combination of basal (primitive) and derived (advanced) traits.

facts.statement: The first Bagaceratops fossils were discovered in the Gobi Desert during the 1970s by a joint Polish-Mongolian expedition.
facts.quote: Los primeros restos de Bagaceratops fueron descubiertos en el Desierto de Gobi durante los años de 1970 por una expedición conjunta polaco-mongola.

facts.statement: Bagaceratops was initially named Protoceratops kozlowskii, later renamed Breviceratops kozlowskii by Kurzanov in 1990, and is now considered Bagaceratops.
facts.quote: Inicialmente se los llamó Protoceratops kozlowskii, y renombrados Breviceratops kozlowskii por Kurzanov en 1990 ahoira se consideran como Bagaceratops.

facts.statement: Bagaceratops is known from five complete skulls and twenty partials showing various life stages, making its growth cycle well understood.
facts.quote: Se lo conoce por cinco cráneos completos y otros veinte parciales en diversas etapas etarias, por lo que su ciclo de desarrollo es bien conocido.

facts.statement: Bagaceratops measured approximately 1 meter in length and weighed an estimated 22 kilograms.
facts.quote: Bagaceratops medía aproximadamente 1 metro de largo, presentando un peso estimado de unos 22 kilogramos.

facts.statement: Bagaceratops had a smaller, triangular tail compared to its close relatives, the Protoceratops.
facts.quote: Poseían una cola más pequeña y triangular que sus parientes cercanos, los protocerátopos.

facts.statement: Bagaceratops lacked frontal horns.
facts.quote: El bagacerátopo carecía de cuernos frontales.

facts.statement: Like all ceratopsians, Bagaceratops was a herbivore that likely ate dominant plants of its time such as ferns, cycads, and conifers.
facts.quote: El bagacerátopo, como todos los ceratopsianos, era herbívoro, alimentándose probablemente de las plantas predominantes de su época, tales como helechos, cicádeas y coníferas.

facts.statement: Bagaceratops was very similar to Protoceratops, possessing a beak but no frontal horns, and a small prominence on the snout.
facts.quote: Los dos dinosaurios eran muy similares, cada uno tenía un pico pero ningún cuerno en la frente, y una pequeña prominencia en el hocico.

facts.statement: Bagaceratops belongs to the family Bagaceratopsidae.
facts.quote: familia: Bagaceratopsidae

facts.statement: The genus Bagaceratops was named by Maryanska and Osmolska in 1975.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Maryanska & Osmolska, 1975

facts.statement: The species Bagaceratops rozhdestvenskyi was named by Maryanska and Osmolska in 1975.
facts.quote: species_authority: Maryanska & Osmolska, 1975

facts.statement: A new family named Bagaceratopsidae has been proposed to include Bagaceratops.
facts.quote: Se ha propuesto una nueva familia para incluirlo, a la que se denominó Bagaceratopsidae.

facts.statement: Bagaceratops lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 80 million years ago in the Campanian stage, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 80 million years ago, en el Campaniaense, en lo que hoy es Asia.

facts.statement: The time range for Bagaceratops is from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Bagaceratops lived in alluvial plain, lacustrine, and aeolian environments under relatively arid to semiarid climates.
facts.quote: The sediments of this formation were deposited in alluvial plain (flat land consisting of sediments deposited by highland rivers), lacustrine, and aeolian paleoenvironments, under relatively arid to semiarid climates.

facts.statement: The Bayan Mandahu Formation, which yielded Magnirostris (now a synonym of Bagaceratops), is considered Late Cretaceous, roughly Campanian.
facts.quote: The Bayan Mandahu Formation, which yielded Magnirostris (now synonym of Bagaceratops), is considered to be Late Cretaceous in age, roughly Campanian.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Bagaceratops should be placed in its own family, Bagaceratopsidae, or remain within Protoceratopsidae.
facts.quote: Se ha propuesto una nueva familia para incluirlo, a la que se denominó Bagaceratopsidae.
